reason: Removes a hardware-timing delay that the driver's documented design keeps on purpose: src/lib/sfx50.6502's header (lines 15-16) says the chip is written 'as the MOS writes it ... with the MOS's delays', and sfx_write's comment says 'as MOS 3.20 writes it (&F5E6)'; the MOS has the same LDY #4 / DEY / BNE settle after write enable goes high. Dropping it changes how the SN76489 is driven on real hardware (the 1 MHz slow-bus port A data and latch line 0), which no emulator proof here can see. The candidate admits this ('a hardware-timing change the emulator cannot show'), and its claim that the chip needs no recovery time after the rising edge is recalled, not measured. That breaks the project's 'Measure, do not recall' rule and rule 1 (same sound as the original on the real machine), and it is a deviation from the driver's agreed design (decision 25) with no decision behind it. Same-length padding (SKIP 5) and the register reasoning (A dead, Y=0 on exit, X kept) do check out, but the timing premise cannot be verified, so it is refuted. Recount: 21 cycles per call saved (LDY #4 2, then 3 x (DEY 2 + BNE taken 3) and DEY 2 + BNE not taken 2 = 19); 0 bytes (5 freed, padded).
